o: Flag each DNA sequence with four boolean patterns: ATG prefix, TAA/TAG/TGA suffix, ATAT anywhere, GGG anywhere. String-matching functions (LIKE, RIGHT, IN) solve it directly.

a.i: Use LIKE with wildcards for substring patterns, RIGHT(...,3) IN (...) for stop codons.
s: Select all columns plus four boolean expressions.

c.python:
SELECT sample_id,
       dna_sequence,
       species,
       (dna_sequence LIKE 'ATG%') AS has_start,
       (RIGHT(dna_sequence, 3) IN ('TAA','TAG','TGA')) AS has_stop,
       (dna_sequence LIKE '%ATAT%') AS has_atat,
       (dna_sequence LIKE '%GGG%') AS has_ggg
FROM Samples
ORDER BY sample_id;

w: In MySQL, boolean expressions evaluate to 1/0 as required. Alternative: REGEXP '^ATG|TAA$|TAG$|TGA$|(ATAT)|(GGG)' split into separate flags. Watch exact column aliases.
